headline: PAGASA Monitors Two LPAs as Habagat Keeps Parts of Luzon Under Heavy-Rain Risk
seoTitle: PAGASA Tracks 2 LPAs, Habagat Rain Risk | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA was monitoring two low-pressure areas on August 28, both with a medium chance of developing into tropical depressions, as Habagat continued to bring heavy rain to parts of Luzon.
deck: One disturbance was east-northeast of Itbayat inside PAR while another formed farther east outside PAR, with both assessed at medium development potential within 24 hours.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA was monitoring two low-pressure areas Friday afternoon as the southwest monsoon continued to bring rain over parts of the Philippines.

As of 2 p.m., the LPA inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility was about 560 kilometers east-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes. A newly formed LPA outside PAR was about 1,460 kilometers east of Central Luzon.

sections.heading: Development potential
paragraphs: PAGASA assessed both disturbances as having a medium chance of developing into tropical depressions within the next 24 hours. Their future tracks and any eventual local cyclone names remained dependent on development and position.

sections.heading: Habagat remains a concern
paragraphs: The southwest monsoon continued to affect Luzon, with heavy-rain warnings issued in several areas during the afternoon. Malacañang suspended government work and classes at all levels in Metro Manila and 16 provinces beginning at 1 p.m. because of the monsoon and the possibility of further enhancement by the LPA inside PAR.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Rainfall-warning colors and LPA positions can change within hours. This report therefore preserves the verified afternoon situation without treating individual warning levels or forecast tracks as fixed beyond their bulletin times.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Saturated ground and swollen waterways can keep flood and landslide risks elevated even when rainfall temporarily weakens, particularly across western and central Luzon.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents should follow the latest PAGASA rainfall warnings, local disaster advisories and any subsequent tropical cyclone bulletins if either LPA develops further.
